title: Wide-comb marbling pattern
subtitle: Using a broad-toothed comb to produce the classic overmarble or Spanish wave
excerpt: The wide-comb pattern is one of the foundational Western marbling designs. A comb with teeth spaced 15 to 25 mm apart is drawn through a stone drop or gel drop base pattern in a single pass, then returned in the opposite direction to produce the characteristic repeated S-curves. The pattern is named 'Spanish' in early pattern nomenclature, though its origin is disputed.
sourceNotes: Richard J. Wolfe, Marbled Paper: Its History, Techniques, and Patterns (1990), chapter on European comb patterns: describes the wide-comb overmarble and Spanish designs as documented in the Augsburg and Venetian marbling traditions from the seventeenth century. Accessible at Internet Archive.

glossaryTerms.definition: A marbling pattern produced by drawing a tool through a base pattern that has already been laid on the size. The overmarble comb moves through and distorts the existing pattern. Distinguished from the original stone or drop pattern that is overmarbled.

A classic overmarble pattern produced by one or two passes of a wide comb through a stone or gel drop base pattern. The characteristic repeated S-curve form. Named 'Spanish' in historical pattern books.

with two passes of a wide-toothed comb. The base pattern must be in place and settled before the comb is introduced. Rushing the comb through before the ink drops have spread to their full diameter produces a compressed and irregular result.

items.name: Carrageenan size, prepared and rested 24 hours
items.notes: Skim the surface of the size with a sheet of newspaper just before laying ink. This removes any surface film or bubbles.

items.name: Marbling inks, 4 to 6 colours
items.notes: Pre-mixed and tested to spread correctly on the size in use. Each colour should spread to a disc 20 to 40 mm across with one drop from a dropper.

items.name: Wide-toothed marbling comb
items.notes: Teeth spaced 15 to 25 mm. The comb should be rigid enough not to flex as it is pulled through the size.

items.name: Alum-treated paper
items.notes: Paper pre-treated with a 15% alum solution and fully dried. The alum mordants the paper surface so marbling ink adheres.

items.name: Marbling tray
items.notes: Slightly larger than the paper sheets. Fill with size to within 2 cm of the rim.

content.text: Lay the stone drop base: drop each colour in concentric rings from the centre of the tray outward. Start with the colour you want to show most in the finished pattern and work outward through 4 to 6 colours. Allow 30 to 60 seconds for the drops to reach their final spread before beginning the comb pass.

Hold the wide comb at one end of the tray with the teeth barely touching the surface of the size. Draw the comb slowly and steadily across the tray from one end to the other in a single pass. The teeth will pull each colour in the direction of the comb, producing elongated S-curves perpendicular to the line of travel. Return the comb from the opposite end to produce a second pass: this deepens the wave and tightens the S-curves. Do not make a third pass: each pass degrades the definition of the curves.

Lower the alum-treated paper onto the size in a rolling motion from one end, without trapping air bubbles. Allow contact for 30 to 60 seconds, then peel the paper from the surface in a single smooth movement. Rinse immediately under cold running water and hang to dry.

items.symptom: The comb drags the ink off the size surface rather than producing curves
items.cause: The ink has dried slightly at the surface, or the comb teeth are dipping too deep into the size.
items.fix: Skim the size surface again with newspaper before laying new ink. Hold the comb so the teeth are no more than 1 mm below the surface as they pass through.

items.symptom: The S-curves are very small and crowded
items.cause: The comb teeth are too closely spaced for the scale of the base pattern drops.
items.fix: Lay the base pattern with larger drops (more ink per drop) or use a comb with teeth spaced 25 mm rather than 15 mm.
